title: Integrated Ops Playbook for Small Teams
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

This playbook consolidates company-wide policies into a concise, actionable reference tailored for small product or platform teams (1–20 people). It focuses on pragmatic workflows for access and permissions, lightweight change management, data handling, procurement and expenses, vendor onboarding, and travel expense processing. The goal is to enable fast, compliant decisions with minimum friction while preserving enterprise controls.

Scope

- Audience: team leads, ICs with budget authority, on-call engineers, people-ops partners, and project managers.
- Applicable to: hosted Redwood services, Dedicated projects, and Private deployment customer work where company policies apply.
- Exceptions: high-risk regulated engagements (HIPAA, SOC-sensitive customers) should follow the full enterprise policy in security-and-compliance.

Principles

1. Minimal friction: default to the simplest approved path for routine actions.
2. Clear ownership: every request or change must have a named owner and an approver.
3. Auditability: actions must be traceable (ticket + ticket ID) and annotated with purpose.
4. Proportional controls: higher impact requires more approvals and evidence.

Section owners and SLAs

- Access & Permissions — Owner: Security & Compliance (security@) — Standard SLA: 48 hours for routine requests, 4 hours for escalations.
- Change Management — Owner: Eng Platform (platform@) — Standard SLA: 24 hours for review, expedited for P0s.
- Data Management — Owner: Data Governance (data-governance@) — SLA: 72 hours for classification decisions.
- Procurement & Expenses — Owner: Finance & Procurement (procurement@) — SLA: 5 business days for standard PO processing.
- Vendor Ops — Owner: Legal / Finance joint — SLA: vendor onboarding 10 business days (standard checks).
- Travel & Reimbursements — Owner: People Ops / Finance — SLA: reimbursements processed within 7 business days after complete submission.

1) Access and Permissions

Quick guide

- Use the self-service portal (internal URL: https://redwood.internal/access) for role-based requests. For CLI users: redwoodctl access request --role <role> --resource <service> --purpose "<short reason>".
- Required metadata for every request: owner (requestor), approver (manager or product lead), ticket ID, business justification, duration (if temporary).

Temporary access policy

- Max duration for temporary elevated access: 14 days. Extension requires documented justification and secondary approver.
- Emergency (break-glass): request via PagerDuty priority workflow and follow up with a retrospective within 24 hours.

Approvals matrix (table)

| Resource sensitivity | Example resources | Approval required | Approver level | Notes |
|----------------------|-------------------|-------------------|----------------|-------|
| Low                  | internal wiki, dev-test S3 | Manager | Team manager | Auto-approve via portal if manager is available |
| Medium               | staging databases, metrics write | Manager + Security | Team manager + Security reviewer | Manual review; may require just-in-time MFA |
| High                 | production databases, PII stores | Manager + Security + Data Governance | Director-level + Security | Requires ticket, rolling window audit, and justification |

Step-by-step access request (recommended)

1. Create an access ticket in JIRA with the tag [access-request].
2. Fill the portal form or run redwoodctl to attach required metadata.
3. Notify your manager for approval. If manager is unavailable, use the delegated approver list.
4. Security performs the review and provision within SLA.
5. If temporary, set an expiration and schedule a review.

2) Lightweight Change Management

When to use the process

- Any change that impacts production services, customer-facing behaviour, or data retention. Small code fixes that do not touch infra configs and pass CI can follow standard PR review without an explicit change ticket.

Minimum change request (CR) template

- Title: short summary
- Owner: who will make the change
- Approver: who will sign off
- Rollout window: preferred and backup windows
- Rollback plan: clear steps to revert
- Impact: affected services and who to notify
- Test plan: how to validate success

Change review tiers

- Tier 0 — Dev-only: No infra or config changes; standard PR review.
- Tier 1 — Low-risk infra: Requires lead + ops read; scheduled deploy window.
- Tier 2 — High-risk/prod-impact: Full change ticket, ops sign-off, and at least one canary rollout.

Emergency changes

1. Follow the incident escalation process.
2. Apply emergency patch with explicit owner and log the action.
3. Create CR retrospect within 48 hours including root cause and permanent remediation.

3) Data Management

Classification and handling

- Classify datasets as Public, Internal, Restricted, or Regulated. Default classification is Internal unless a dataset contains PII or regulated content.
- Retention windows: adherence to the Data Retention Policy is required:

| Classification | Example | Retention default |
|----------------|---------|------------------|
| Public         | marketing assets | indefinite unless superseded |
| Internal       | telemetry, docs | 3 years |
| Restricted     | user emails, account metadata | 7 years or as required by contract |
| Regulated      | PHI/PCI | per contracts and legal; do not store unless authorized |

Data access controls

- Sensitive datasets require RBAC via the central data catalog. Requests must include a dataset owner and a business justification.
- Encryption at rest is mandatory for Restricted and Regulated datasets.

Data handling checklist (template)

1. Dataset name and owner
2. Classification (Public/Internal/Restricted/Regulated)
3. Retention schedule (date or rule)
4. Access list and provisioning method
5. Audit logging enabled? (Y/N)

4) Procurement and Expenses

Decision thresholds and approvals

- <= $2,000: team manager approval (P-card use encouraged).
- $2,001–$25,000: manager + finance review; use standard PO.
- > $25,000: manager + procurement + legal; must have a business case.

Preferred vendors and process

- Use approved vendor list in procurement portal. For new vendors, follow the Vendor Onboarding Checklist (see Section 6).
- Create a PO request in the procurement system with cost center and GL code. Attach quotes and justification.

Expense reporting guidance

- Use the expense portal and include scanned receipts for all transactions. Per diem and meal caps follow the Travel policy below.
- P-card reconciliation: submit receipts within 10 business days of purchase.

5) Vendor Management (Onboarding + Offboarding)

Vendor onboarding checklist (minimum items)

1. Vendor name, legal entity, and contact details.
2. Scope of work, deliverables, and SLAs.
3. Risk assessment: data access, network access, and subprocessors.
4. Contract signed by Legal with appropriate NDAs and data protection language.
5. Security review: vulnerability disclosure, access method (VPN, IP allowlist), and credential management.
6. Finance setup: W-9 / tax form, payment terms, and PO number.
7. Technical onboarding call and knowledge transfer.

Ongoing vendor reviews

- Quarterly check-ins for vendors with privileged access or > $50k ARR.
- Annual security questionnaire for all vendors that touch production data.

Offboarding steps

1. Revoke all credentials and termination of network access.
2. Confirm return/deletion of company data and purge access tokens.
3. Close financial accounts and finalize outstanding invoices.

6) Travel and Expense Policy (Concise)

Booking and approvals

- Use the corporate travel portal for booking. Manager approval required for trips > 2 days or international travel.
- Preferred booking windows: 21 days prior for standard fares; use corporate travel agents for exceptions.

Spending caps and allowable expenses

- Hotel: up to $300/night in major markets (exceptions with prior approval).
- Meals: $75/day domestic, $125/day international.
- Ground transportation: use Uber for local rides; airport car service for arrivals/departures when > $100.

Expense submission template (required fields)

- Trip purpose, dates, approver, cost center, itemized receipts, and policy justification for any cap exceptions.

7) Lightweight Templates (copy/paste into ticket descriptions)

Access request template:
Title: Access request — [resource] — [short reason]
Owner: [Name] | Approver: [Name]
Resource: [service or dataset]
Role requested: [role]
Duration: [start – end]
Justification: [business purpose]
Ticket: [JIRA-1234]

Change Request template:
Title: CR — [service] — [purpose]
Owner: [Name] | Approver: [Name]
Rollout window: [date/time]
Rollback: [steps]
Impact: [users/services]
Test plan: [smoke checks]
Ticket: [JIRA-1234]

Vendor onboarding short form:
Vendor: [legal name]
SOW summary: [3-line summary]
Data access required: [Y/N]
Contact: [email / phone]
Procurement ticket: [PO-1234]

Expense submission checklist:
- Receipt attached (Y/N)
- Cost center assigned (Y/N)
- Approver signed off (Y/N)

8) Exceptions and Escalations

- Any exceptions to these playbook items must be submitted as an exception request to security@ with an explicit owner and a sunset date.
- Escalation path for unresolved policy disputes: team manager -> department head -> People Ops -> COO.

Appendices

A. Useful internal commands and URLs
- Access portal: https://redwood.internal/access
- CLI: redwoodctl access request --role <role> --resource <service> --purpose "reason"
- Procurement portal: https://redwood.internal/procure
- Expense portal: https://redwood.internal/expenses

B. Lightweight checklist cheat-sheet (one-pager)
- I need access: ticket + portal + manager approval -> Security provisions within 48h.
- I need to buy <$2k: P-card or manager approval -> reconcile within 10 days.
- I need vendor: complete onboarding checklist before sharing any data.

C. Contacts and escalation list
- Security & Compliance: security@redwood.com
- Procurement & Finance: procurement@redwood.com
- People Ops: people-ops@redwood.com
- Eng Platform (change): platform@redwood.com

Document maintenance

This playbook will be reviewed annually and after major incidents. Suggested updates should be submitted via the documentation PR workflow and include reviewer signoff from relevant owners.

End of document
